summary: Applying a blank spellbook matches C through item selection, then JavaScript refuses the entire flip_through_book call. C apply.c:flip_through_book describes flipping pages, reports an empty book when sighted, and makes that book type known. Its other source branches handle underwater, blindness, hallucination, the Book of the Dead, a novel, and spellbook ink fading. The missing owner is this whole function and the doapply spellbook dispatch.

source.branch: For a sighted, nonhallucinating Wizard above water applying SPE_BLANK_PAPER, doapply calls flip_through_book, which prints the page-flipping message, then the blank-book message, calls makeknown for the type, and returns ECMD_TIME. Underwater returns ECMD_OK before flipping; the entire function also handles Book of the Dead sensory messages, blind pages, hallucination, novels, and studied-book fadeness.
callers: apply.c:doapply selects SPBOOK_CLASS and returns flip_through_book(obj) at lines 4237-4238; js/apply.js:doapply currently throws UnsupportedApplyError for that class.
dependencies: objnam.c:thesimpleoname supplies the printed item name; preserve its existing display semantics.
o_init.c:makeknown changes object-type discovery in the blank-paper arm; use the ported canonical discovery helper.
pline.c:You_hear, You_see, You_feel and hcolor affect Book of the Dead sensory messages; message behavior remains source-conditioned by Deaf, Blind and Hallucination.
